basic_identification.full_title: Guidelines for Use of Vehicles for Collection and Transportation of Municipal Solid Wastes — Part 2: Maintenance (First Revision)
basic_identification.sector_category: Chemical / Environmental Protection and Waste Management (approved by the Chemical Division Council and finalized by the Environmental Protection and Waste Management Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Environmental Protection and Waste Management Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard (Part 2) specifies procedural and safety guidelines for the regular, preventive, and corrective maintenance of specialized and general-purpose municipal vehicles (including compactor trucks, auto-tippers, dumper placers, hook loaders, and refuse collectors) used to collect, compact, and haul municipal solid waste (MSW) to protect equipment from corrosive leachate and guarantee structural safety.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Procedural Guidelines / Code of Practice (Environmental Protection / Municipal Waste Vehicles)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Procedural Guidelines Standard. Compliance with IS 12662 (Part 2) is verified through municipal audits, state-level urban development departments, Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM) clean city star ratings, and state pollution control boards. While there is no direct BIS 'ISI Mark' stamp for IS 12662 itself, compliance with its daily, weekly, monthly, and chemical disinfection schedules is universally mandated in public municipal collection and transport tenders across India. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.

requirements.detail: Requires daily inspection of all critical vehicle systems before starting collection routes. This includes engine fluids, coolant levels, tyre pressures, brake systems, steering gear, and a thorough visual check of all hydraulic hoses, hose couplings, and valves for leaks.

To prevent vector breeding (flies, mosquitoes), severe foul odours, and the buildup of highly corrosive organic municipal solid waste, the entire vehicle body—particularly the collection hopper, compaction chamber, and chassis underside—must be washed daily with high-pressure water jets.

Following high-pressure washing, the vehicle's waste containment compartments must be disinfected daily using approved disinfectants and germicides (such as sodium hypochlorite, phenol, bleaching powder, or quaternary ammonium compounds) to safeguard public health and protect conservancy workers.

Requires weekly inspection of leachate collection tanks, seals, and drainage valves. Valves must be flushed, and tanks emptied at designated disposal points. Because municipal organic waste leachate is highly acidic (typically pH 4.0 to 6.0), any bare steel or peeling paint must be cleaned immediately and treated with protective anti-corrosion, rust-preventive paint coatings.

All moving joints, bin-lifter hinges, hydraulic cylinder pivot pins, tailgate locking linkages, and sliding guide tracks must be greased weekly to prevent mechanical wear, friction buildup, and premature component seizing.

Checks of hydraulic oil levels, oil quality, suction filters, pressure relief valve settings (via standard pressure gauges), and hydraulic pump mounting bolts must be performed monthly to ensure consistent compaction forces and prevent sudden high-pressure hose bursts.

Safety equipment must be checked. Rear loading hoppers, heavy tailgates, dumper derrick arms, and container pins must feature functional mechanical safety locks/pins. Audible reversing alarms, beacon lights, reflective safety tape, and cabin warning flashers must be tested daily.

Maintenance files must demonstrate that all conservancy and workshop staff are provided with and wear proper Personal Protective Equipment (heavy-duty rubber gloves, safety goggles, face shields, protective aprons, safety boots, and masks) during cleaning, lubrication, or mechanical repairs.

Mandates that a permanent daily maintenance logbook be maintained inside the driver's cabin or workshop tracking fuel consumption, dynamic compaction cycles, lubrication dates, hydraulic filter changes, and part replacement histories.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 12662 (Part 2) : 2025 (First Revision) is the national Indian Standard specification and code of practice establishing guidelines for the maintenance of municipal solid waste (MSW) collection and transport vehicles. Formulated under the Environmental Protection and Waste Management Sectional Committee, this standard regulates the preventive, regular, and corrective maintenance procedures for compactor trucks, refuse collectors, auto-tippers, and container carriers. To counter the highly corrosive effects of organic waste leachate and prevent vector breeding in cities, the standard mandates a strict maintenance regime—enforcing daily high-pressure water washing, daily chemical disinfection, weekly greasing of all moving joints and hydraulic pivots, weekly flushing of leachate tanks, and monthly hydraulic system pressure checks—to ensure structural roadworthiness and protect the health of conservancy workers.
